sections.html: Hoplias malabaricus is one of the most widespread species of tetra in South America; it is therefore suspected that it is more likely to be a number of externally very similar, so-called cryptic species. German-bred offspring are now available. They are currently 6-8 cm long and quite compatible with each other, provided there is enough food.
The parent fish are wild-caught from Brazil (unfortunately no closer catching area is known).
The aquarium is furnished with coarse sand, roots and robust plants (Cryptocoryne crispulata var. balansae).
The water values in the breeding tank: temperature 26°C, pH 6 to 7.5 (they have spawned at scarcely pH 6). Hoplias otherwise have no big demands on the water values.
The breeding animals are fed with smelt, sprats, mussels and worms, but meat is also popular.

Hoplias are very calm fish, lurking hunters who do not move much. The male guards the nest and takes care of the brood. This can lead to quarrels between the parents. The male is very aggressive and irritable in this time.
The male is about 30 cm long, the female 28-29 cm.
The offspring was bred from a pair of wild-caught fish. The male is 2.5-3 years old, the female about 2 years; the animals were not acquired together, but at intervals of about half a year.
